meta.date: Recorded by Moroni after AD 400, of words spoken at the first appearing
meta.unit: The words of Christ on giving the Holy Ghost (Moroni 2)
principles: Words given to twelve while a crowd stood by
A gift passed on by hands and by name
A record supplied because the crowd could not hear

world_behind.title: This is the promise Mormon made in 3 Nephi
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 18:37 breaks off to say the multitude heard not the words spoken when Jesus touched the disciples, and that he would show hereafter that the record of it is true. This chapter is what he meant, and it is his son who supplies it.

world_behind.title: The twelve are named in another book
world_behind.text: Verse 1 calls them the twelve whom he had chosen and gives no names. 3 Nephi 19:4 lists all of them, including Nephi's brother Timothy, so the men receiving this authority are identifiable from elsewhere in the record.

world_behind.title: One moment is reported twice, by two writers
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 18:36 has him touch them one by one with his hand; verse 1 here has him lay his hands upon them and gives the words. Mormon recorded the act and Moroni recorded the speech.

world_behind.title: The apostles at Jerusalem are the stated pattern
world_behind.text: Verse 2 closes with "for thus do mine apostles." 1 Nephi 12:9 distinguishes those twelve from these, and 3 Nephi 12:1 has Christ present the Nephite twelve as ministers to this people. The instruction ties a practice here to one on the other side of the world.

world_behind.title: The condition comes before the power
world_behind.text: Verse 2 puts mighty prayer first and the ability second. Moroni 3:2 puts prayer before the ordination and Moroni 4:2 before the sacrament, so all three practice chapters open the same way.

world_behind.title: The chapter is three verses long
world_behind.text: Moroni 2 through 5 run three, four, three, and two verses. Mormon 8:5 says Moroni has no ore and no room left on the plates, which is the physical reason these procedures survive as forms rather than as scenes.

words.text: Those taught by and following a teacher. Treated at 3 Nephi 5:13. The record uses the word fifty-three times and the King James Bible two hundred and forty-four.
The number of the chosen. The record uses the word thirty-two times and the King James Bible a hundred and eighty-eight.
Picked out from among others. It appears thirty-eight times in the record and a hundred and twenty-three in the King James Bible.
Strong, or done with full force. Treated at 1 Nephi 4:2. Verse 2 attaches it to prayer rather than to a person or an act of power.
Those sent out with authority. The record uses the word thirteen times and the King James Bible sixty. Verse 2 is the one place the Nephite record cites their practice as a pattern.
The crowd, as distinct from the twelve. It appears eighty-six times in the record and two hundred and forty-three in the King James Bible.
Came down upon. Treated at 1 Nephi 2:7. Verse 3 uses it of the Holy Ghost coming on those who were touched.

phrases.term: The words of Christ, which he spake unto his disciples
phrases.text: Moroni's heading for the chapter. The chapter is the quotation.

phrases.term: The twelve whom he had chosen
phrases.text: Who was being addressed. 3 Nephi 12:1 gives the same count and the same choosing.

phrases.term: As he laid his hands upon them
phrases.text: When the words were spoken. The touch and the instruction happen together.

phrases.term: And he called them by name
phrases.text: The one detail Moroni adds before the quotation. Names come before office.

phrases.term: Ye shall call on the Father in my name, in mighty prayer
phrases.text: The first instruction. Prayer comes before the power is mentioned.

phrases.term: After ye have done this ye shall have power
phrases.text: The order set on the two. Verse 2 makes the power conditional on the prayer.

phrases.term: To him upon whom ye shall lay your hands, ye shall give the Holy Ghost
phrases.text: What the power is for. The same gesture that was used on them is used by them.

phrases.term: And in my name shall ye give it
phrases.text: The requirement on the giving. The name governs both ends of the chapter.
The precedent cited. Acts 8:17 records the practice in Jerusalem.

phrases.term: The multitude heard it not, but the disciples heard it
phrases.text: Why this chapter exists. 3 Nephi 18:36 and 37 report the same moment from outside.

phrases.term: On as many as they laid their hands, fell the Holy Ghost
phrases.text: The result, given in one line. It reports the instruction working.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: Words held back twelve chapters
verses.text: 3 Nephi 18:37 reports the touching of the twelve and then says "the multitude heard not the words which he spake," adding, "I will show unto you hereafter that this record is true." Moroni 2 is that hereafter. The volume withheld the words at the scene and supplies them in the appendix.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: Named first, empowered second
verses.text: "And he called them by name" (v. 2), a phrase that occurs nowhere else in the volume. The instruction that follows makes the power conditional and sequential: call on the Father in mighty prayer, "and after ye have done this ye shall have power." The record puts the gift not in the hands but in what precedes them.

cites.quote: And he called them by name

spans.text: And he called them by name

verses.label: v. 3
verses.title: The crowd is told what it missed
verses.text: The record states its own audience boundary, "the multitude heard it not, but the disciples heard it," and then hands the reader what the multitude was denied.

chapter.title: The chapter is a quotation with a frame
chapter.text: Verse 1 introduces, verse 2 quotes, verse 3 reports the outcome.

chapter.title: The touch comes with the words
chapter.text: Verse 1 has him speaking while his hands are on them.

chapter.title: Names come before office
chapter.text: Verse 2 has him call them by name before he says what they will do.

chapter.title: Prayer is the first step and the power is the second
chapter.text: Verse 2 makes the order explicit with an after.

chapter.title: The gesture is handed on
chapter.text: Hands were laid on them in verse 1 and they lay hands on others in verse 2.

chapter.title: His name governs both ends
chapter.text: Verse 2 has them pray in his name and give in his name.

chapter.title: A precedent outside this record is cited
chapter.text: Verse 2 says thus do mine apostles, pointing away from the Nephites.

chapter.title: Moroni supplies what the crowd missed
chapter.text: Verse 3 says the multitude heard it not. 3 Nephi 18:37 reports the same gap from the other side.

applications.title: The hands convey an assignment
applications.text: The chapter's subject is words spoken while hands were laid on the twelve, and everything that follows is instruction about what they are to do. Nothing in the passage is about standing.

applications.title: Call people by name
applications.text: The instruction begins with him naming each of the twelve.

applications.title: Pray before you expect power
applications.text: The verse puts the asking first and the ability second.

applications.title: Pass on what was done to you
applications.text: Hands were laid on them, and they were told to lay hands on others.

applications.title: One audience heard it and one did not
applications.text: The multitude heard it not, and the disciples heard it. Being present at something is not the same as being addressed by it.

applications.title: Write down what only you heard
applications.text: The multitude missed it, and Moroni preserved it decades later.

questions.text: Whom has someone chosen and taught, in my case?
Do I use people's names, or only their roles?
What am I expecting to be able to do without asking first?
What was given to me that I am meant to hand on?
What have I heard that others in the room missed?
What do I know that would be lost if I did not write it down?
